messages:
incident-bot: Pager: increased 5xx rate detected in nw-region ingress proxy (502/504 spike). Service-level threshold breached (5m error rate > 8%). Auto-escalation to on-call: Maya K.
Maya K.: acked. joining bridge -> https://redwood.zoom/incident-6391023456 :wave:
Maya K.: quick summary? what’s the scope of impact (routes/customers)?
incident-bot: Context: spike started at ~6391023300. Top source: proxy-nw-ingest-0/1/2. Error distribution: 68% 502 gateway, 24% 504 downstream timeout, 8% 500. Affected routes: /v1/generate (high), /v1/chat (medium). Top 5 tenants by volume flagged (internal list).
Jorge L.: on it. pulling proxy and gateway logs now. checking pool sizes + conntrack.
Claire R.: Support reporting ~30 customers seeing elevated errors, some on mobile. CS is ready to send holding message if we need customer comms.
Maya K.: throttle/circuit breakers? did any self-heal occur before I joined?
Jorge L.: No automatic recovery yet. Observed growth in queue latency and upstream worker 504s. Looks like an ingress proxy thread starvation pattern — connections opening faster than backend drains.
Alex P.: any recent deploys to nw? I saw a config roll earlier from eng-release but not sure which services.
Jorge L.: checking deploys... deploy-bot shows: no prod deploys to proxy clusters in last 2h. There was a model-serving config change 3h ago but in eu region.
Maya K.: step 1: scale ingress proxy pool (add nodes) and reduce new connection rate via emergency prio limits. Jorge, can you run scale and increase backpressure?
Jorge L.: doing. CLI:
```bash
# scale ingress pool
redwood infra scale --cluster proxy-nw-ingress --replicas +4 --reason "incident 6391023456"
```
Jorge L.: also bumping conn limit on proxy to allow more upstream concurrency:
```yaml
# temp override
proxy.conn_limit: 12000 -> 20000
proxy.max_inflight_per_src: 500 -> 300
```
Maya K.: note: reduce max_inflight_per_src to throttle noisy tenants; that should help fairness.
incident-bot: Action logged: scaled proxy cluster +4 nodes (req id: act-6391023461).
Jorge L.: scaled, nodes starting. health checks pending. traffic will rebalance once instances ready.
Maya K.: while nodes spin up, enable fallback routing to eu-west for low-latency tolerant routes. Claire, any regulatory concerns for these tenants?
Claire R.: most affected are not region locked; we can fail over to eu-west for 60m as temporary mitigation. inform customers in CS notes.
Alex P.: applying emergency route steer:
```bash
redwood route update --from nw-region --to eu-west --match "/v1/generate" --pct 30 --reason "egress overflow"
```
Alex P.: roll started. +30% traffic now to eu-west for /v1/generate.
Jorge L.: incoming error rate has dropped 20% since initial scale + route steer. 502s still present but tail latency improving.
Maya K.: good. watch QPS and 99th perc latency. set alert if >10% error in next 5m.
incident-bot: Alert rule created by Maya K.: email oncall@redwood if error_rate > 10% for 5m.
Jorge L.: noticed spike in backend worker mem usage correlated with the traffic bump. likely GC thrash on some ML-workers. marking as secondary issue.
Maya K.: let's drain the two suspicious worker nodes then pin them to older JVM flags. Jorge, initiate graceful drain for ml-worker-17/18.
Jorge L.: draining ml-worker-17,18. command: `redwood node drain ml-worker-17 --timeout 300s`
incident-bot: drain started. estimated drain complete ~120s.
Alex P.: CS update draft: "We are aware of elevated 5xx rates for some NW-region requests. Engineers are actively mitigating (scaling, routing). Some requests may be temporarily routed to eu-west. We’ll update within 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:
Claire R.: approve. add note: "no persistent data loss observed".
Maya K.: agreed. publish.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to SRE lead in 8m if error rate not <8%.
Jorge L.: drain complete on ml-worker-17, failing health check on ml-worker-18; investigating. root cause looks like a memory leak in a third-party library after sustained 1000+ concurrent sessions.
Maya K.: if ml-worker-18 is unhealthy, continue to evacuate and terminate. We need to ensure not to cause cascade by terminating too many at once. Maintain min-healthy >= 60%.
Jorge L.: terminating 18, launching replacement with tuned flags. launched ml-worker-18-v2 with patched GC flags.
Maya K.: monitoring metrics. error rate now down to 6%. Good. keep route steer at 20% for next 15 minutes then reassess.
Alex P.: customer impact: CS reporting reduction in tickets, mobile reports less frequent. sending interim update to affected customers now.
Claire R.: Logging note: we saw an uptick in a particular upstream host 10.12.4.23 returning 502 with payload "upstream read timeout". added to exclusion list for routing.
Jorge L.: excluded host 10.12.4.23 from pool, rebalanced. per-proxy errors dropped further.
Maya K.: summary for postmortem: cause = combo of ingress connection surge + a memory regression in ml-worker causing reduced backend capacity; mitigation = scaled proxy, emergency per-src throttle, route-steer to eu-west, drained unhealthy workers and patched GC flags, excluded bad upstream host.
Maya K.: action items: 1) roll patch to ml-workers in nw region (owner: Jorge) 2) add early mem/leak detection alert to worker fleet (owner: SRE) 3) revisit conntrack/conn_limit defaults for proxy (owner: Infra) 4) customer comms template refinement (owner: Claire)
Jorge L.: I’ll open the follow-up tickets and start a hotfix rollout.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2 by Maya K. Incident duration so far: 8m.
Alex P.: any handoff? I have to go in 20m. Maya, can you take point for the next 30m if it flaps?
Maya K.: yes, I’ll stay. Jorge, if error rate >8% again, trigger full cross-region failover and call for broader pager.
incident-bot: Incident closed by Maya K. at 6391023750 (status: mitigated).
Maya K.: closing notes: monitoring for 60m. will author postmortem and link follow-up tickets. thanks all for quick coordination :heart:
Claire R.: nice work everyone.
Alex P.: thanks :thumbsup:
Jorge L.: closing logs and will attach findings to ticket 6391023456-pt1.
